description: Workers whose workplace is San Francisco County by county of residence and means of transportation to work (toSF), and SF-resident workers by county of workplace and mode (fromSF). Counts of workers 16+ (persons, one usual commute each; not trips).

sources.title: American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year Public Use Microdata Sample, California person file (psam_p06.csv)
sources.method: Tabulated here from microdata: workers = JWTRNS not blank; weight PWGTP; residence county from PUMA (2020 PUMAs; every PUMA in the listed counties lies in one county per the 2020 tract-to-PUMA file); workplace county from POWSP=006 + POWPUMA (in California the 2020 POWPUMA code is county FIPS x 100, e.g. 07500 = San Francisco; confirmed because every worked-from-home worker's POWPUMA matched their residence county). Mode: JWTRNS 01 with JWRIP=1 -> droveAlone, JWRIP>=2 -> carpool; 02 bus; 03 subway/elevated; 04 long-distance/commuter rail; 05 light rail/streetcar/trolley; 06 ferry; 07 taxi/ride-hail, 08 motorcycle, 12 other -> other; 09 bike; 10 walk; 11 wfh. moe90 = 1.645*sqrt(4/80*sum((rep_i-est)^2)) over replicate weights PWGTP1-80 (Census successive-difference replicate method).

sources.role: alternate, pre-pandemic, published table (no MOE in this copy)
sources.publisher: MTC/ABAG Vital Signs (data.bayareametro.gov), repackaging AASHTO CTPP 2012-2016 Table A302103
sources.title: Vital Signs: Commute Patterns - Bay Area (dataset c33n-96bi), last updated April 2020
sources.period: ACS 5-year 2012-2016 (CTPP); flows between the 9 Bay Area counties and all California counties (non-CA residences excluded by MTC)
sources.method: Published CTPP residence-county x workplace-county x means (A302103) counts; CTPP values are rounded (to 5, small cells to 4). Carpool = 2/3/4/5-6/7+ person carpool; transitBus = "Bus" (ACS then: bus or trolley bus); transitLightRailStreetcar = "Streetcar or trolley"; transitSubwayElevated = "Subway"; transitCommuterRail = "Railroad"; other = taxi + motorcycle + other. Light rail was not a separate ACS category before 2019.

sources.title: Vital Signs: Commute Patterns - Bay Area (2022) DRAFT (dataset j7ht-u3pq), updated July 2022
sources.period: ACS 5-year 2016-2020 PUMS (national person file, per MTC)
sources.method: MTC tabulation; geography limited to 9 Bay Area counties + "Rest of CA" + "Outside CA" (so Santa Cruz/San Joaquin/Sacramento are inside otherCalifornia here). Same field mapping as the CTPP alternate.

sources.role: totals only (no mode), all origins incl. out of state, with MOE
sources.title: 2016-2020 5-Year ACS Commuting Flows, Table 1 (sorted by residence) and Table 2 (sorted by workplace)
sources.method: Rows with residence or workplace = 06075 extracted; otherCalifornia/outsideCalifornia are sums with MOE combined as root-sum-of-squares (approximation).

fields.total: all workers 16+ in the flow, including worked from home
fields.transit: transitBus + transitRail + transitFerry (ACS public transportation excl. taxi)
fields.transitCommuterRail: ACS "Long-distance train or commuter rail" (Caltrain, ACE, Capitol Corridor, Amtrak)
fields.transitLightRailStreetcar: ACS "Light rail, streetcar, or trolley" (Muni Metro, F-line, cable car, VTA LRT)
fields.wfh: worked from home; ACS places their workplace at home, so wfh is only nonzero in the San Francisco->San Francisco cell
fields.sampleRecords: unweighted PUMS person records in the cell

checks.note: Published-table figures copied from server/beta3/reference/acs-commute.json (ACS 2020-2024 5-year summary file). PUMS and summary-file estimates differ slightly by design (PUMS is a ~2/3 subsample with its own weights).

notes: toSF/fromSF are the ACS "usual mode last week" of persons (one commute per worker), not daily trips. Convert to trips with attendance/telework factors separately.

Worked-from-home workers are placed at their home, so a person living in Alameda who teleworks for an SF employer is NOT in toSF. Cross-county wfh is 0 by definition; the SF->SF wfh cell (143,562 in 2020-2024) is SF residents working at home.

2020-2024 pools pandemic years (2020-2021 had very high WFH and low transit). Cross-county commute volumes are well below the 2012-2016 CTPP values (e.g. Alameda->SF 67,246 vs 99,355; transit 35,219 vs 60,930). Use alternates.ctpp2012_2016 for a pre-pandemic baseline and the primary block for a recent pooled estimate.

toSF covers California residents only (the PUMS California file). Out-of-state residents working in SF: about 8,619 implied for 2020-2024 (ACS B08604 SF workplace total 621,656 minus PUMS CA-resident sum 613,037, mixing two estimates), and 7,017 (MOE combined approx.) in the Census 2016-2020 flows table. No mode split for them in the primary block; mtc_pums2016_2020.toSF.outsideCalifornia has one (6,811).

otherCalifornia = all other CA counties (and multi-county PUMAs/POWPUMAs, none of which include a listed county). fromSF.outsideCalifornia = SF residents working out of state (POWSP != 006), including abroad.
Small cells are noisy: check moe90 and sampleRecords (e.g. Santa Cruz->SF n=25, Napa->SF n=81). Zeros in PUMS cells mean no sample record, not a true zero.

Mode is self-reported and only the mode used for the longest distance is recorded. Rail sub-modes can be misreported (e.g. some BART riders choosing light rail, Muni Metro riders choosing subway); transitRail is the robust total.

ACS 2019+ splits light rail/streetcar/trolley from bus and renamed railroad to long-distance/commuter rail; 2012-2016 CTPP uses older categories (bus or trolley bus, streetcar or trolley car, subway or elevated, railroad), mapped to the same field names.
SF->SF figures: PUMS 383,315 vs ACS table B08007 384,949; fromSF sum 464,721 vs B08301 466,388; consistent within sampling error.
notFound: CTPP 2017-2021 Part 3 flow tables (e.g. B302103/A302103 for 2017-2021): ctpp.transportation.org returned HTTP 403 to a plain request and the data portal ctppdata.transportation.org is a JavaScript app gated by reCAPTCHA, so it was not used (no workaround attempted). The same flows were tabulated directly from 2020-2024 PUMS instead.

Census county-to-county commuting flow tables (2011-2015, 2016-2020) have totals only, no means of transportation; used only for totals (alternates.censusFlowsTotals2016_2020). No newer release (2017-2021 or later) was found on census.gov.
Mode split of out-of-state residents commuting to SF for 2020-2024 (would need the national PUMS person files; not downloaded to keep the job light).
MOEs for the MTC/CTPP alternates (the MTC copies omit them).
